items.title: Pre-US Open Brief · Gold won back more than half its morning loss and sits at 4,042.3. Nasdaq futures are flat. The euro slipped to 1.1221 after weak euro-area surveys. Brent oil touched $115.00 on reports of possible new US and Israeli strikes on Iran

Pre-London Brief · AI fears sank tech on Thursday, and money rushed into US government bonds. The 10-year yield had its biggest one-day drop since March 2023, to about 4.95%. Gold still fell more than 2% and touched 4,000.9 this morning. Nasdaq futures are flat after a 2.9% drop

Pre-US Open Brief · A broad risk-off morning. Brent oil is up 2.5% to $111.59 on new Gulf tanker strikes, Nasdaq futures are down 1.7% as Tesla and Meta revived AI-spending doubts, and gold is down 1.45% to 4,089.8 even as money floods into US Treasuries

Pre-US Open Brief · Oil is back in charge. Brent hit $111, a five-month high, and the expiring November US oil contract jumped 5%. Gold broke this morning's floor, Nasdaq futures slid to a new low, and the euro gave back its Asian gain
Pre-London Brief · Wall Street's chip bounce did not travel. Korea's KOSPI is down 4.3%, gold slipped for the first time in three sessions to near $4,160, and the euro is quietly clawing back
Pre-US Open Brief · The Monday bounce is holding but leaking. Nasdaq futures are still up about 1%, gold is stuck just under $4,200, and France's riots pushed the euro below Friday's close
